newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index ends up after late selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index ends up after late selective buying.

text.p: The Jakarta stock index ended stronger on the back of selective buying of some secondaries and heavyweight Telkom in late trading, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index rose 2.63 points, or 0.46 percent, to closed at 570.66 points after touching an intra-day low of 567.87 points in morning session. Gainers led losers by 47 to 46, with 63 counters unchanged.

"Although the market focus remained on the initial public offering of Bank Negara Indonesia, some brokers started collecting selected stocks and it helped the index to gain further," a foreign broker said.
But brokers said market was likely to be mixed on Monday as a firm direction in the market was unlikely because the market's attention will be on the primary market.
"Today's trading volume was relatively small and I don't expect much changes in the coming week. At least until the BNI's IPO finishes," one local broker said.

The largest state-owned bank BNI will start the four days offer next Monday, ahead of its November 25 listing in Jakarta and Surabaya stock exhanges. BNI will float around 1.1 billion shares at an offer price of 850 rupiah per share.
Property firm Ciputra Development topped the active list with 3.6 million shares traded, rising 125 rupiah to 1,825 on what brokers said was fresh buying after the firm's presentation on Thursday.
Banking stock BDNI was actively traded, rising 50 rupiah to 1,700 rupiah on a volume of 2.8 million shares traded on what brokers said was fresh buying.
They said some investors had their eye on certain banking stocks ahead of next week's BNI float.
"Some investors are starting to look at other bank stocks which have earnings-per-share ratios relatively close to BNI's," one local broker said.
A foreign broker said it was also due to the limited allotment of BNI so they have to switch the fund reserved to same sector.
The country's largest retailer Matahari was also eyed by some buyers due to its relatively cheap price, brokers said.
"Confidence towards the firm is also increasing as they have slowed down their expansion programme," a foreign analyst said.
Heavyweight Telkom rose 50 rupiah to 3,525 rupiah on a volume of 902,000 shares on local-led buying, brokers said.

They said it was due to a company announcement to give incentives shares to Indonesian shareholders who had kept their shares since November 2, 1995 and will not sell-off their holdings before November 14, 1996.
Telkom said in a statement that incentives shares will be from government's stake and there are expected to be about 3 million shares on offer.
"The maximum incentives shares for individual investors will be 50 shares and 500 shares for institutions or cooperatives," it said.
